name: Grace Yilmaz

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI firms or government, and your answers stay confidential. What is a normal working day like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I drive a loader at a large mine, mostly on the early shift. I do the walk-around, check the tyres and hydraulics, then move rock until the radio sends me somewhere else. I like knowing the machine by its sound; the paperwork at the end of a muddy shift is what wears me out.

say: I say **operators** still have to listen to equipment and take responsibility for a safe shift.
I welcome **small savings** from routine reports if a person checks the figures.
think: I still worry about **mortgage payments** even if AI changes very little.
I know **four months** of savings would go quickly if winter shifts were cut.
do: **Keep** driving the loader on my assigned shifts and check the overtime board each week.
**Save** the usual amount from each payday before buying the older child a bicycle.
feel: **Steady**, though the mortgage still puts a knot in my stomach.
S0.quote: A decent operator still hears a change in the engine before a warning light comes on.
fieldNote: **Work pride** rests on hearing and judging a machine, rather than on filling in a report.
**Household caution** predates AI; four months of savings does not erase concern about weaker shifts.

steps.text: Keep driving the loader on assigned mine shifts
Put the usual amount from each payday into savings

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At the pit I would say we should stop pretending every new screen can drive a loader. A decent operator still hears a change in the engine before a warning light comes on.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I would be relieved about the machines, but the mortgage still goes out every month. We have roughly four months of expenses saved, and a slow quarter at the mine could eat that without any AI at all.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep my loader shifts and the same household budget for now. I would put the usual amount into savings each payday and check the overtime board before agreeing to another expense.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Mostly steady, with the usual knot about the mortgage. My children are growing out of their clothes faster than our savings grow.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you delay first if shifts fell?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The older child needs a new bicycle, and I would wait until we know whether the winter shifts hold. I would tell both children that we buy things when we can pay for them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does any routine AI touch your day?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The shift report might be filled in faster, but I still sign it after checking the load figures. I would not trust a tidy report over the machine in front of me.

say: I think **planning software** may help the office, while operators still need to watch the ground.
I want **experienced drivers** testing any robot before managers count on fewer people.
think: I fear **clerks** could lose tasks before the crew loses driving hours.
I worry **crew numbers** may shrink once robots prove useful, putting my mortgage under pressure.
do: **Ask** the shift lead about joining a machine trial this month.
**Learn** new equipment controls during paid shifts in the first year.
**Redirect** one subscription payment into mortgage overpayments while hours are uncertain.
feel: **Anxious** about hours, with some confidence that I can learn proven equipment.
S1.quote: A trial with a driver watching the machine is how I decide whether it works.
fieldNote: **Trial first** is her condition for accepting new equipment, consistent with her steady approach to change.
**Office colleagues** are visible to her as people, while she worries that later automation could reduce her own shifts.

steps.text: Learn the new equipment controls on paid mine shifts
Redirect one subscription payment into mortgage overpayments

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the crew that planning software might clear some office work, but it will not move rock by itself. If robots come in slowly, I want the experienced drivers there when the new kit is tested.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I suspect the planners and clerks get squeezed first, then management starts counting how many drivers a shift needs. I have seen a neat schedule on a screen turn into a mess when weather closes one ramp.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I would ask the shift lead to let me sit in on a machine trial, if there is one. In the first year of those changes, I would learn the new controls on paid shifts and move one small subscription payment into mortgage overpayments.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy for our office people, and anxious for my own hours if the company uses slower robots to trim crews. I can learn controls, but I cannot replace a whole pay packet with confidence.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which colleague comes to mind?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Laila, who sorts our shift sheets, has two children too, and much of her work is checking and booking. I would tell her what I hear from the shift lead, not pretend the office is safe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: You want a trial but distrust screens; how do those fit?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A trial with a driver watching the machine is how I decide whether it works. If it misses a hazard, I want that written down before anyone calls it ready.

say: I expect **reports and schedules** to change by 2028, while loader work faces the later 2031 robots.
I say **three years** gives a mortgaged family little room for a failed transition.
think: I suspect **office savings** could become spending on driverless machines after thinking AI arrives.
I know **four months** of savings would not support a long search if loader shifts disappear.
do: **Ask** the training supervisor about maintenance apprenticeships and their fees now.
**Take** an evening maintenance course after 2028 only if the household can pay without borrowing.
**Pay** extra toward the mortgage when loader overtime appears.
feel: **Anxious** about possible lost hours around 2031 and the household bills due before then.
S2.quote: Four months of savings will not carry us through a long search.
fieldNote: **Date distinction** is clear: paperwork and scheduling in 2028, physical loader work around 2031.
**Training condition** matters; she will study only if fees can be met without a loan.
**Family calendar** turns an abstract three-year gap into mortgage and school costs.

steps.text: Take an evening maintenance course if fees require no borrowing
Pay extra toward the mortgage when loader overtime appears

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the 2028 thinking machines will change our reports and schedules before they change the cab. The 2031 robots worry me more; three years is short when a family owes on a house.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think the company could save money in the office by 2028 and spend it on driverless machines later. By 2031, if those machines really handle our ground, my hours could go sharply down. Four months of savings will not carry us through a long search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting now I would ask the training supervisor what maintenance apprenticeships accept experienced operators, and I would check the fees before signing anything. In the first year after 2028 I would take an evening maintenance course only if we can cover the fees without borrowing, and pay an extra amount toward the mortgage whenever overtime appears.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious once I thought about 2031. Three years sounds long until I put school fees, food and mortgage dates on the same calendar.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your partner?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my partner we cannot count on loader overtime lasting into 2031. We would go through the mortgage statement together on Sunday, not frighten the children with dates they cannot control.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the course is too expensive?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep asking the mine for training on paid time and keep the overtime money in the house account. I will not take a loan for a course that might not lead to work.

say: I welcome **five years** to thinking AI, though my loader still faces robots around 2034.
I want **training places** before the mine brings in machines that can drive.
think: I could reduce **mortgage debt** during the extra years if overtime holds.
I fear **nearby vacancies** may be crowded with other operators if several mines change together.
do: **Request** a written maintenance training route from the supervisor this year.
**Save** the next two overtime payments for course fees.
**Enrol** after 2031 if a local course has space and mine shifts still pay the bills.
feel: **Anxious**, with a plausible route if the training place and wages both hold.
S3.quote: A friendly promise at the gate cannot pay for an evening class.
fieldNote: **Written dates** are her test of whether the mine will support a worker through change.
**Conditional enrolment** depends on an available place and continued wages, not mere interest.
**Local alternatives** exist, but she expects competition from other miners.

steps.text: Save two overtime payments for local course fees
Enrol after 2031 if course space and mine wages hold

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years until thinking work changes is a fairer warning than two. The loader would still face capable robots around 2034, so I would want training places before the mine orders them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The extra years let us bring the mortgage down, but I would not call the job safe. If my partner keeps working, we can probably manage an evening course while I still draw mine wages. I worry about trained workers all chasing the same few nearby jobs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the training supervisor this year for a written path into equipment maintenance, then save the next two overtime payments for course fees. In the first year after 2031, I would enrol if a local course has a place and the mine still pays my shifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, though I can see a route that was missing in the fast picture. A plan feels real only when the course has a place and the bills are covered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why ask for it in writing?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A friendly promise at the gate cannot pay for an evening class. I want dates and fees that I can put beside the mortgage statement.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Suppose maintenance also gets automated?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would use what I learn to inspect faults and safety stops while people still run the fleet. If that work dries up too, some similar mines nearby give me somewhere else to ask, though no offer is guaranteed.

say: I could use **a decade** to plan if the mine shares its equipment intentions.
I see **2036 paperwork** and later 2039 loader robots as separate changes to my work.
think: I could have choices at **age 56** if the mortgage balance is lower by then.
I cannot assume **pension timing** will let me leave early.
do: **Review** mortgage balance, savings and school costs with my partner each November.
**Check** overtime changes after 2036 as automated schedules arrive.
**Take** a paid maintenance refresher if the mine offers one.
feel: **Uneasy** about the eventual machine change, but more settled with time to prepare.
S4.quote: I like the crew and would rather finish work on my own terms than bet the house on an early exit.
fieldNote: **Long horizon** changes her mood because mortgage reduction becomes plausible before physical robots arrive.
**No early exit** is promised; she insists on a real pension calculation and an open nearby job.
**Annual review** ties family costs to the mine schedule instead of relying on distant predictions.

steps.text: Keep driving assigned loader shifts this year
Make one extra mortgage payment if loader overtime has been good
Take a paid mine maintenance refresher if offered

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the crew a decade lets us prepare properly, provided the mine tells us what it plans. The paperwork can change in 2036, and the hands-on loader work has until around 2039 before those robots arrive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 53 when the thinking AI comes and about 56 when capable robots reach the cab. If the mortgage is much smaller then, I could choose shorter hours or another mine rather than grab any job. But I would not promise myself a pension date I have not earned.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I would keep my shifts and set a yearly mortgage review with my partner. In the first year after 2036, I would check how the automated schedules affect overtime, and take the mine maintenance refresher if paid time is offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: More settled than in the shorter pictures. I would still watch the order book at the mine, because ten years can be wasted just as easily as two.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does a yearly review look like?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner and I would put the balance, savings and school costs on one sheet each November. If overtime has been good, we would make one extra mortgage payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave the mine early?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if the numbers at 56 make sense and a nearby job is actually open. I like the crew and would rather finish work on my own terms than bet the house on an early exit.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the path from new office systems to driverless loaders would be so short. A maintenance apprenticeship with clear fees and paid time at the mine would help more than a speech about being flexible. I need to know whether my family can carry the mortgage while I learn.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask what the mine will tell families before it buys machines. My children do not need every rumour from a shift bus, but my partner and I need enough warning to decide what we can pay for.

headlineQuote: My children do not need every rumour from a shift bus, but my partner and I need enough warning to decide what we can pay for.
portrait: **Grace, 43**, drives a loader at a large mine and trusts the sound of equipment as much as any screen.
**Four months** of savings and a mortgage leave room for small plans, while school-age children keep household costs close.
**Proven training** appeals to her, especially maintenance work with written dates, affordable fees and paid time.
**Fast AGI** worries her because 2028 office change could lead to 2031 driverless machines before the family has adjusted.
**Longer warning** lets her reduce debt and weigh nearby mines, though she will not assume an early pension.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** gives too little time between new office systems and capable loader robots around 2031.
whatWouldHelp: **Paid maintenance training** with clear fees would let her learn while keeping mortgage payments covered.
**Early mine notice** about equipment purchases would let her family plan before rumours spread.
